spec.alternative_hypothesis: The lagged BAA10Y change (basis points, latest available at the decision close) has a positive coefficient in the daily BAA10Y->TYVIX partial lead-lag regression (spread widening predicts higher next-day TYVIX log changes), with partial R-squared at least 0.005 and a positive holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared. Note on wording: the planner draft's 'positive, out-of-sample component' refers to positive incremental explanatory power (incremental R-squared above zero), not to a positive coefficient — the expected coefficient sign is positive on the economic argument in the mechanism, independently of that wording.
spec.benchmark: Own-history baseline: next-day TYVIX log change predicted from its own lagged log change and the lagged VIX common-factor control only, without the lagged BAA10Y change
cost_assumptions: TYVIX is a volatility index and is not tradable; there is no listed TYVIX futures contract
Treasury-volatility exposure through options on Treasury futures has no clean free price series from which transaction or roll costs could be measured
The cost gate is therefore informational, not a verdict criterion; the holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared carries the economic weight
The reported gross sign-rule edge applies no costs at all and is an upper bound on any tradable edge
spec.cost_model: Informational only (study 003's precedent for a volatility-index target): TYVIX is not tradable; there is no listed TYVIX futures contract, and Treasury-volatility exposure through options on Treasury futures has no clean free price series from which costs could be measured. The trial reports the gross sign-rule edge on holdout out-of-sample augmented forecasts (1x, always invested while positioned, no costs applied) as an informational upper bound on any tradable edge, with a block-bootstrap confidence interval; the holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared carries the economic weight. The cost gate is not a verdict criterion.
exclusions: Bars outside the sample window (2003-01-02 to 2020-05-16) are out of sample; TYVIX is discontinued after 2020-05-15, so no post-2020 data exists for the target.
Incomplete synchronized rows are excluded and counted.
FRED empty-field missing values are excluded at fetch time and counted.
The first two panel return rows have no lagged BAA10Y change and are dropped.
The naive unlagged alignment, the no-factor control, the reverse placebo and the sub-period stability split are descriptive only and are not in the test family.
known_confounders: BAA10Y is defined as the BAA yield minus the 10-year Treasury yield (DGS10); the spread change nets out the rates level by construction, so a common rates shock moves both legs and is differenced out — the predictor measures the credit-specific component. The DGS10 leg is therefore not a separate control.

TYVIX is itself a rates-volatility measure, so the rates-level channel is partly the mechanism under test rather than a confounder to control: a rates shock that moves both the spread and rates volatility is the transmission the hypothesis describes, not a bias to remove.

The 2-trading-day BAA10Y availability lag is verified behaviorally (6b evidence probe 2026-11-18T21:45Z plus the fetch-time re-check) and assumed constant across the sample. If the historical posting lag differed, the predictor alignment is wrong for those periods.
FRED series are revised over time; the fetch records the current vintage. Historical values as first published may differ from the current vintage (revision risk is unmodelled).

The VIX control is itself a FRED series with the standard 1-trading-day publication lag; the control uses the latest available VIX change (lagged 1 step), not the same-day change, so it cannot absorb the day-t common shock in full.

The sample covers the 2008 crisis and the 2020 COVID crash and ends at TYVIX's discontinuation (2020-05-15); transmission may be regime-dependent and the conclusions do not extend past 2020. Sub-period stability is descriptive only.

TYVIX log changes are close to unpredictable (study 003's base-model R-squared for next-day VIX log changes was about 0.012); the baseline explains little, so the incremental R-squared is measured against a weak baseline.

The PIT store records available_at equal to the event time (adapter limitation); the publication lag is enforced in the trial's panel construction via the study-007 lagged-changes module, not in the stored observations.
spec.mechanism: A widening BAA credit spread reflects rising credit risk premia and tightening financial conditions: corporate funding costs rise relative to Treasuries as default risk is repriced. Stress in credit markets typically coincides with rising rates volatility, as Treasury yields reprice on flight-to-quality flows and shifting rate expectations, and as the same risk-off impulse lifts implied volatility across asset classes. The spread is an end-of-day published signal, so any transmission should appear the next trading day. The expected sign is positive: spread widening predicts higher next-day TYVIX log changes.
spec.missing_data_policy: No forward filling; drop incomplete synchronized rows and report the dropped count. FRED empty-field missing values are excluded at fetch time and counted.
model_definition: Partial lead-lag OLS with Newey-West HAC standard errors (daily lagged BAA10Y change -> next-day TYVIX log change)
Purged walk-forward out-of-sample evaluation of the primary model (baseline: own history plus lagged VIX control; augmented: plus lagged BAA10Y change)
Naive lead-lag scan (lags 0-5, raw Pearson correlations) as a descriptive upper bound (not in the test family)
Descriptive only: unlagged (naive) alignment, no-factor upper-bound control, reverse placebo (TYVIX->BAA10Y), sub-period stability

Cost gate is informational only (study 003's precedent): the gross sign-rule edge on holdout out-of-sample augmented forecasts, no costs applied, with a block-bootstrap confidence interval — not a verdict criterion
spec.multiple_testing_family: Credit-spread transmission to rates volatility (1 test: daily lagged BAA10Y change -> next-day TYVIX log change)
spec.null_hypothesis: Lagged BAA10Y changes have no incremental predictive value for next-day TYVIX log changes over TYVIX's own history and the lagged VIX common-factor control, with dependence controls.
spec.primary_metric: Partial R-squared of the lagged BAA10Y change (bp, latest available at the decision close) in the daily BAA10Y->TYVIX partial lead-lag regression
rejection_criteria: Holm-adjusted primary p-value at or above 0.05
Holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared at or below 0
spec.research_question: Does the most recent BAA10Y credit-spread change available at the close predict the next-day TYVIX log change beyond TYVIX's own history and the lagged VIX common-factor control?
spec.target_definition: Next-day TYVIX log change (FRED VXTYN, CBOE TYVIX history); the predictor is the most recent BAA10Y level change in basis points available at the decision close — under the verified 2-trading-day BAA10Y posting lag, the change ending two trading days before the decision close.
spec.title: Credit-spread changes lead rates volatility (TYVIX)
